candidates.title: Decide each arithmetic operation's precondition scope from its own domain, not by analogy to sibling operations
candidates.body: When adding a new operation to POST /calculate (or any future arithmetic op in this API), decide whether it needs a PreconditionError-guarded domain restriction (like div/mod's b === 0 zero-divisor check) by examining that operation's own mathematically undefined/invalid input region -- never by defaulting to, or mechanically copying, an existing sibling operation's precondition set. An operation with no genuinely undefined native-semantics input region (e.g. pow under IEEE-754 **) gets no precondition; one with a real undefined region (e.g. div/mod's zero divisor) does. Absence of a precondition must be a deliberate, explicit statement in Change Context/Brief, not a silent omission.
candidates.rationale: (1) Extraction provenance: this change's Brief (X4, NFR1) and Change Context §6 explicitly state pow gets no zero-divisor-style PreconditionError, in deliberate contrast to div/mod's established pattern from the prior initial-calculator change -- the Brief calls this out specifically so later NFR/OCL work does not over-generalize the div/mod pattern onto pow. (2) Reuse: this project's operation set is evolving one operation at a time (add/sub/mul/div/mod, then pow); any future addition (e.g. sqrt, log, root) faces the identical judgment call of whether to inherit a precondition, so the criterion (domain-driven, not analogy-driven) is directly reusable across those changes. (3) Non-obvious boundary: the natural engineering instinct when adding a new op alongside div/mod is to also add an input-validation precondition 'for consistency', even where none is mathematically warranted; this pattern makes explicit that precondition scope is a per-operation domain judgment, not a house style applied uniformly across all operations -- which is exactly the over-generalization this change's Brief was written to head off.

candidates.title: Green contract tests do not prove a new operation is reachable through the HTTP dispatch/whitelist layer
candidates.body: Contract-level tests against module logic (e.g. Calculator.pow, calculate()) exercise business logic directly and can pass fully even when the HTTP layer (src/server.ts) never routes the new operation value to that logic -- e.g. because a hand-maintained request-validation whitelist (an OPERATIONS Set/array) was not updated to include it. Passing unit/contract tests are not sufficient evidence that a new operation is actually callable end-to-end over the real transport. Verify with an HTTP-layer test that sends a real request for the new operation and asserts success, and confirm the test's sensitivity with a mutation spot-check: temporarily remove the new value from the whitelist, rerun, confirm the HTTP test (and only that test) now fails, then restore.
candidates.rationale: (1) Extraction provenance: this change's first-pass integration verification found all contract tests green for pow, but no automated check exercised src/server.ts's HTTP request-validation whitelist -- pow had not been added to the OPERATIONS Set, so it was unreachable over real HTTP despite fully passing contract tests. Critique flagged this as a scope gap; the fix added tests/http/server.test.ts, and re-verification independently reproduced the mutation spot-check (removing "pow" from the whitelist made exactly the new HTTP test fail, 17/18 vs 18/18) to confirm the gap was genuinely closed rather than merely asserted. (2) Reuse: this repo's whitelist-then-dispatch shape at the HTTP boundary (a validation list gating access to per-operation logic) is a recurring integration seam for every future operation or route addition, not specific to pow; the mutation-spot-check technique (deliberately break the code path a test claims to cover, confirm the test catches it) generalizes to any change that tags a check as 'covering' a given behavior. (3) Non-obvious boundary: a fully green contract-test suite is easy to mistake for full end-to-end coverage; this gap was invisible from contract-test output alone and surfaced only by explicitly exercising the transport layer -- future Briefs/WorkPlans should require an HTTP-layer check whenever a change adds a new dispatchable value behind a whitelist/switch, and should prefer mutation-style verification over trusting a verification report's 'covers' tag at face value.

skipped_reasons: NFR5's additive-only op-enum-extension constraint (never remove/narrow an existing enum value, route, or schema) is standard API-compatibility discipline restated for this change; not proposed as a separate knowledge node because it carries no domain-specific non-obvious boundary beyond ordinary additive-API practice any competent API team would already apply -- tautological in this context.

Native JS ** (IEEE-754) edge-case semantics for pow (0 ** 0, NaN, Infinity, very large exponents) are left unhandled per this change's open_questions -- a one-off §5 tech-selection / edge-case deferral scoped to this change, not a reusable cross-change Means. Could become knowledge only if a future change deliberately tightens or hardens pow's edge-case behavior.

PreconditionError and the div/mod zero-divisor pattern are vocabulary/behavior originating from the prior initial-calculator change, not this one; add-power-operation's Brief/Context raise no new neighbor-confusion or scope risk about that term specifically, so no concept node is proposed here on this change's behalf. Flagging as a knowledge/ gap: this project has no knowledge/ directory yet at all, so a retroactive seed harvest against initial-calculator (covering PreconditionError, the div/mod precondition contract, and other core calculator vocabulary) is recommended as separate, deliberate future work rather than being folded into this change's harvest.

pow's reuse of the existing calculate() response shape (no new JSON fields) is explicitly marked 'deferred to OpenAPI apply' in this change's open_questions -- not yet a settled contract detail and not a Means-level judgment criterion, so not harvested.

Tooling gap: scripts/solidsdd-kg.sh build --root . failed with 'open .../.solidsdd/kg/schema.yaml: no such file or directory' -- this project has no .solidsdd/kg/ at all yet (consistent with there being no knowledge/ directory either), so 'promote suggest --json' could not be run. This harvest was produced entirely from filesystem reading of the change's artifacts (change-context.md, change-brief.json, integration-verification-report.json, critique-integration-verification-report.json) rather than CLI-assisted suggestion; cli_suggest is omitted rather than fabricated.

Apply-time note (both candidates applied, gate-approval.json scope: knowledge_harvest, decision: approve): knowledge/{concepts,policies,patterns,decisions,lessons}/ and .solidsdd/kg/{config.yaml,schema.yaml,links.yaml} were created for the first time in this project (config.yaml/schema.yaml copied unmodified from examples/inventory-reservation's kg scaffold, the only precedent in this repo). Both nodes were hand-authored as Markdown under knowledge/patterns/ and knowledge/lessons/ (frontmatter id/type/title/status:active/maturity:canonical/scope/facets/verified_at + body from each candidate's `body` field). `scripts/solidsdd-kg.sh build --root .` and `check --root .` now run successfully (nodes=35, edges=1, parse_issues=0; check exit 0, only pre-existing unrelated REQ_MUST_HAVE_IMPL/REQ_MUST_HAVE_VERIFY warns for both changes' requirements, no errors) -- the earlier schema-build failure was purely 'no .solidsdd/kg/ yet' and is resolved now that the scaffold exists. One downstream link was written to .solidsdd/kg/links.yaml: derives_from add-power-operation/R5 -> LES-CONTRACT-TESTS-MISS-HTTP-DISPATCH. No link was written from add-power-operation/R2 to PAT-OPERATION-PRECONDITION-SCOPE: this repo's shared schema.yaml restricts derives_from's `to` type to [policy, invariant, requirement, decision, lesson, concept], which excludes `pattern` -- a requirement can currently link to a lesson/policy/decision/concept via derives_from but not to a pattern under this schema. Flagging as a follow-up schema gap rather than forcing an invalid edge; PAT-OPERATION-PRECONDITION-SCOPE's provenance is still carried via its own source_refs and body text.
